name: Alarus CH 2000
variants: SAMA CH2000 (military surveillance, Iraqi Air Force)
summary: All-metal two-seat trainer designed by Chris Heintz, built in Canada as the Zenair CH 2000 and in Florida as the AMD Alarus.

wings: Low cantilever wing with no struts
engines: Single Lycoming flat-four in a blunt cowl
fuselage: Wide two-seat side-by-side cabin under a large glazed canopy
tail: Conventional single fin and rudder with a low horizontal tail

tellTales: All-metal two-seat low-wing with a wide, roomy cabin and large glazing
Plain constant-chord wing on fixed tricycle gear
Blunt, simple nose on a trainer-type airframe

confusedWith.howToTell: The XL-2 has a sleek composite fuselage and a large bubble-like windscreen; the Alarus is plainer, with an all-metal skin and a blunter nose.
The PA-28 is a four-seater with a long fuselage; the Alarus is a compact two-seater.
The DA20 has a T-tail and composite skin; the Alarus has a conventional tail and riveted metal skin.
